title: Save manually before every choice
body:
The game autosaves often, but the autosave can land after the choice. Make a **manual save** before an important conversation or before starting a job: if you don't like the outcome, reload and try another option.

- You can save from the menu almost any time you are not in combat.
- There are **20 manual slots**, 20 autosave and 10 quicksave slots: use several instead of always overwriting the same one.
- With Nintendo Switch Online you get cloud saves, and CDPR's cross-progression keeps another copy.
- Since 2.5, saves are grouped by playthrough, and on Switch 2 the insufficient-space error when saving no longer appears.

title: Your perks can be redistributed; your attributes, only once
body:
A build is not final: from the character menu you can **refund perk points** for free, one by one, whenever you want. **Attributes**, on the other hand, can be reset **only once per character**.

Try perks freely and keep the attribute reset for a big build change. Make a manual save before using it.

title: Why won't the ripperdoc sell me the double jump (Reinforced Tendons)?
body:
**It's your level, not your Street Cred: Reinforced Tendons go on sale from level 10.** There is no Tier 1 version; the lowest is Tier 2.

- Ripperdocs stock cyberware by your level only. None of it needs Street Cred: the "Street Cred 12, €$45,000" in old guides predates 2.0.
- The same goes for every Legs implant (Lynx Paws, Fortified Ankles) and Arms implant (Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire), and for Memory Boost, Optical Camo, Kerenzikov and Synaptic Accelerator: all from level 10.
- From level 1 you can already buy RAM Upgrade, Smart Link and Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics.
- While you go from level 5 to 10, save about €$11,000: Tier 2 costs around €$10,700.

title: How much do Reinforced Tendons cost, and how much money should I save?
body:
**About €$10,700 at Tier 2, the tier sold from level 10 to 19.** Two 2.x guides agree on that figure, but neither shows the price on screen: check it in game.

- Cyberware price depends on the implant's tier, not on your level: it costs the same at level 10 as at 19.
- With Charles Bucks's discount (20%, if you accept his bribe in the gig Last Login) it drops to about €$8,600. Street Cred takes up to another 15% off.
- The €$45,000 in old guides is a 1.x price, and IGN's €$67,824 looks like its Tier 4 price.
- Upgrading it later takes 1.5 times the components of a normal implant.

title: I used to see a cheap implant and now only a pricier one shows up. What happened?
body:
**At levels 10, 20, 30 and 40 the ripperdoc switches implant tier: the old version disappears and the next, pricier one appears.** Only one tier of each implant is on sale at a time.

- If you want something at Tier 1 (Smart Link, RAM Upgrade, Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics), buy it before you reach level 10.
- The stock and its random bonuses only change every 10 levels, not every day.
- What you already installed never drops a tier: you raise it yourself with components at the ripperdoc.
- Every ripperdoc has the same stock, so looking at another one doesn't help.

title: I can't install an implant: it says I don't have enough cyberware capacity.
body:
**Your Cyberware Capacity grows 3 points per level. If it isn't enough, swap one implant for another, level up or look for capacity shards.**

- You have 36 capacity at level 5 and 51 at level 10. What you already wear (Viktor's implants and the Militech Paraline) takes about 22, so you have about 14 free at level 5 and about 29 at level 10.
- Typical costs: Reinforced Tendons 8, RAM Upgrade 8, Smart Link 4, Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics 2, Memory Boost 18 and Optical Camo 20.
- More capacity: Cyberware Capacity Shards (random drops from level 2), the Engineer skill at its levels 10 and 30, and the Technical Ability perks Renaissance Punk and Edgerunner.

title: Why won't the ripperdoc let me upgrade an implant? Should I upgrade mine or buy a new one?
body:
**To upgrade an implant you need crafting components of the right tier and eddies; if either is missing, the option won't go through.** There seems to be no level requirement for upgrades: the game data sets none.

- Components come from disassembling weapons and clothes, and from loot. In the Crafting menu you can turn 5 components of one tier into 1 of the next.
- Lucky Day (Technical Ability 9) gives +25% components from looting.
- Almost all cyberware goes up to Tier 5++, which needs Phantom Liberty (included in the Ultimate Edition).
- Upgrading the implant you already have is usually the better deal: buying the next tier costs a lot more. That is a deduction from the prices, not an official figure.

title: Where do I buy quickhacks? Yoko sells me almost nothing.
body:
**Before level 7, Watson's netrunner vendors only have Ping, apparently Bait, and crafting specs. Tier 2 quickhacks appear when you reach level 7.**

- In Watson, quickhacks are sold by **Yoko Tsuru** (EdgeNet, Kabuki Market) and **Nix** (Afterlife, Little China), with the same list. It is not confirmed that Nix trades with you before The Heist.
- The other netrunner vendors, such as Chang Hoon Nam in Japantown, are Act 2.
- Tier 2 quickhacks from your level 7, Tier 3 from 15 and Tier 4 from 23. Per the game data, a higher-tier cyberdeck unlocks them earlier.
- No vendor stocks Tier 1 Short Circuit or Overheat: those come from loot, enemy netrunners and access points.
- With the spec and quickhack components you can craft them yourself.

title: Should I pay Viktor now? What happens if I don't?
body:
**There is no deadline and no penalty: Viktor just won't sell or install anything until you pay him the €$21,000.**

- Watson's other four ripperdocs (Charles Bucks, Dr. Chrome, Instant Implants and Cassius Ryder) sell the same stock at the same price, so the debt barely gets in your way.
- The story doesn't force you to pay him.
- Spend first on what you need: Reinforced Tendons at level 10 (about €$10,700) and your RAM implants. Pay Viktor when you have money to spare.
- When you pay, Viktor will try to refuse the money and V will insist. The wiki lists no reward for it.

title: How do I make money fast in Watson?
body:
**Do the NCPD Scanner Hustles, the five Cyberpsycho Sightings and Regina's gigs, and sell what you don't use.**

- **Watson NCPD hustles:** €$750–2,100 each, about €$42,000 in total, plus the loot in their caches.
- **Act 1 cyberpsychos:** €$2,300–2,900 each, about €$13,000 for all five.
- **Regina's gigs:** the five tier 1 gigs pay about €$14,000; Last Login, €$6,400.
- **Access points:** Breach Protocol gives eddies.
- Sell junk at Drop Points and to vendors.

The figures are wiki values and may vary with your level. Car races (€$10,000 each) are Act 2. Don't use duplication tricks: none is confirmed for 2.5.

title: How do I upgrade an iconic weapon like Dying Night?
body:
**In the Crafting menu, on the Upgrades tab, with the weapon in your inventory: stashed ones don't show up.** Each upgrade raises one tier and costs crafting components; it needs no perks or specs.

- Since 2.0 only iconic weapons (and cyberware) can be upgraded. Normal weapons can't: replace them with higher-tier ones.
- It costs 75 components of the current tier to reach "+" and 40 of the next tier to go up a tier. The last step, to 5++, costs 200 Tier 5.
- Upgrading, crafting and disassembling give Engineer skill XP.
- Since 2.1 you can mark a weapon as a favorite so you don't sell or disassemble it by mistake.

title: Does clothing give armor? Where do I put spare stuff when I'm overloaded?
body:
**Since 2.0 clothing is mostly cosmetic: armor comes from cyberware.** Wear what you like and put what you don't use in the stash.

- Your apartment's Wardrobe keeps the look of every clothing item you pick up: you can sell or disassemble the clothes and keep using their look. Since 2.0 you can also open it at clothing vendors.
- Your apartment stash is the same one as your cars'. Update 2.5 added filters to it.
- Your base carry capacity is 200. Raise it with the Titanium Bones implant (Skeleton, from level 1) or with the Solo skill at its levels 5 and 25.
- Guides that rank clothes by armor or talk about clothing mods predate 2.0.

title: Can I buy a car or a motorcycle yet? Where did my car go?
body:
**You can, but it isn't worth it yet: spend on cyberware first.** Cars are bought on AUTOFIXER, a netpage you open on V's computer or at terminals at gas stations and repair shops.

- Per rpgsite and the wiki, before The Heist there are only four cars, with no Street Cred requirement: Thorton Galena G240 (€$13,000), Mahir Supron FS3 (€$16,000), Thorton Colby C125 (€$18,000) and Villefort Columbus V340-F Freight (€$19,000). Other sources say sales open later: check it.
- The cheapest motorcycle, the Brennan Apollo (€$30,000), needs Street Cred 12 and looks like Act 2.
- Your Archer Hella is removed at the start of Act 2 and comes back after Delamain's job Human Nature. After The Heist you also get Jackie's ARCH for free.

title: What is Street Cred for in 2.x?
body:
**For discounts at every shop (up to 15%), to unlock cars on AUTOFIXER and, in 2.5, for the job Welcome to Paradise.** It doesn't change ripperdoc stock and doesn't open gigs.

- Discount: −1% at Street Cred 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30; −2% at 35 and 45, and −5% at 50, the maximum.
- Welcome to Paradise needs The Heist done and Street Cred 15.
- Since 1.5 gigs need no Street Cred: they arrive in sets as you finish the previous ones.
- Ripperdoc cyberware depends only on your level.
- Reaching max Street Cred gives the achievement Legend of the Afterlife.

title: My smart weapon won't lock on to enemies. What do I do?
body:
**You need a Smart Link in the Hands slot, and Viktor's Ballistic Coprocessor sits there: swap it at any ripperdoc.** Skippy is the only one that locks on with nothing.

- Smart Link is sold from level 1, costs 4 capacity and gives +1 or +2 RAM.
- In Act 2, the Tyger Claws tattoo (free from Cassius Ryder after The Gig) also enables lock-on and takes no capacity.
- Check that the weapon really is Smart: Power and Tech weapons never lock on.
- Rounds can miss: the target must be inside the tracking box, and against Tyger Claws they miss 50% of the time.
- Reloading or switching weapons breaks the lock until you have Acquisition Specialist and Target Lock Transfer (Intelligence 15).

title: It won't let me cast a quickhack. Why?
body:
**It's almost always RAM: the quickhack costs more than you have left, or more than your maximum.** Synapse Burnout costs 10 and your Tier 1 Militech Paraline has 5.

- RAM comes back on its own, slowly: out of combat, one unit per minute. Optimization (Intelligence 4) speeds it up by 35%.
- For a quickhack that costs more than your maximum you need more RAM (RAM Upgrade, Intelligence, another cyberdeck) or Overclock.
- You generally have to see the enemy, directly or through a camera.
- Some enemies resist quickhacks and cost more RAM.
- Hack Queue (Intelligence 9) is what lets you put two quickhacks in a row on the same enemy.
- Breach Protocol no longer works on enemies: since 2.0 it only works on access points.

title: What is trace, and how do I make them stop tracing me?
body:
**Combat and Control quickhacks are traceable: casting them fills a trace bar and, if it completes, enemies know where you are.** Covert quickhacks almost never trace, and Ping never does.

- **Encryption** (Intelligence 4): −30% traceability on all your quickhacks.
- **Shadowrunner** (Intelligence 9): every takedown wipes trace progress.
- **Memory Wipe** and **Sonic Shock** are untraceable; Memory Wipe also reduces trace out of combat.
- With Tier 5 System Collapse, neutralizing an enemy netrunner removes all trace.
- With the Arasaka cyberdeck, enemies take longer to trace you.
- Per players, getting away from the spot also helps.

title: An enemy netrunner is hacking me and I see a progress bar. What do I do?
body:
**Break their line of sight (hide or destroy the cameras they use) or damage them: damage interrupts their hack.**

- The scanner marks netrunners with their own icon: take them out first, or quickhack them before they finish.
- **Counter-A-Hack** (Intelligence 9, after Hack Queue) lets you hack them through walls and obstacles, at 1 RAM less. **Copy-Paste** spreads the counter-hack to their allies.
- **Self-ICE** (Frontal Cortex, from level 20, capacity 5) blocks one enemy quickhack on its own and recharges in 45 to 20 seconds, depending on its tier.
- In Act 1, the simplest fix is to hide or shoot the netrunner.

title: What is Overclock and how do I activate it?
body:
**It's the Intelligence 15 netrunner mode: for 14 seconds you cast quickhacks even without RAM, and each missing unit costs 10 Health.** Its cooldown is 30 seconds.

- It's the Overclock perk, which needs Embedded Exploit. The mode unlocks at its **level 3**; levels 1 and 2 only give bonuses.
- **You need a cyberdeck in the Operating System slot.** If you swap it for a Sandevistan or a Berserk, you lose quickhacks and Overclock: you can't have both.
- Per one guide, on a controller you activate it by pressing L1 + R1 (PlayStation) or LB + RB (Xbox) together; on Switch 2 it should be L + R. Check it in Settings → Controls.
- At level 5 you are many points short: expect to have it around level 15–20.

title: I can't find the option to carry two pistols.
body:
**You need Cool 9 and the 2.5 perk Double Trouble.** It only works with Power pistols and revolvers: not with smart weapons (Skippy) or Tech ones.

- Then, in the inventory, set a Power pistol or revolver as your primary weapon: a secondary weapon slot appears on the left.
- You can mix a pistol and a revolver; you don't need two of the same.
- Each gun deals −37.5% damage, and both fire together.
- From Act 1 you have Dying Night and, in The Heist, Kongou.
- For a hacker it's an extra: it uses no smart rounds.

title: How do I knock someone out without killing them?
body:
**Grab them from behind without being seen and pick the non-lethal option. In combat, use blunt weapons, your fists or a weapon with the Pax mod.**

- Lethal weapons can also incapacitate if you avoid weak points.
- **Don't hit them once they're down:** with a Pax weapon, hitting an unconscious target kills them. Per players, explosives, katanas and knives always kill.
- System Collapse (Tier 4 Ultimate quickhack) knocks them out without a sound.
- In Cyberpsycho Sightings the pay is the same, but Regina is grateful at the end if you keep them alive.
- Skippy, in Puppy-Loving Pacifist mode, aims at limbs (Act 2).

title: Why do I deal so little damage? What does the red skull mean?
body:
**Since 2.0 enemies level up with you: what counts is the weapon's tier, not your level.** Swap your Tier 1 weapons for Tier 2 ones as soon as you reach level 9.

- Tier 2 weapons from your level 9, Tier 3 from 17 and Tier 4 from 25.
- Normal weapons can't be upgraded; iconics, like Dying Night, can.
- Some enemies have Low, Medium or High armor, and smart weapons hit softer since 2.0.
- For a hacker, quickhacks do the damage: Embedded Exploit (Intelligence 9) gives +60% against targets under Control or Covert quickhacks.
- **The skull**, per 2.x players, marks an elite enemy: more health and more damage, and some can't be grabbed, but they can be killed. Scan them and use quickhacks and cover.
- You can lower the difficulty any time.

title: How do I turn invisible? Why did Optical Camo take away my grenades?
body:
**Optical Camo (from level 10) makes you nearly invisible for a few seconds, and it takes the same Combat Gadget quickslot as grenades: you use one or the other.**

- It costs 20 capacity, lasts 4 to 7 seconds and recharges in 70 to 50, depending on its tier.
- To get grenades back, swap that quickslot in the inventory (a deduction; check it). Hacker alternative: the Detonate Grenade quickhack.
- Before level 10: move crouched, use Distract Enemies, switch cameras off or use them, and do takedowns from behind.
- Cool perks: Feline Footwork, Killer Instinct, Ninjutsu and Vanishing Act.
- Ping (free from Yoko) reveals the network; Memory Wipe, Sonic Shock and System Collapse are untraceable.

title: Why do my heals and grenades have a cooldown?
body:
**Since 2.0, health items and grenades have charges that recharge on their own over time; they aren't used up.** No source gives the base number of charges: check the item's description.

- **Glutton For War** (Technical Ability 4): each enemy neutralized instantly recharges 5% of your health items and grenades.
- **Health Freak** (Technical Ability 9): they recharge faster and, at its level 2, you get one more health item charge.
- Since 2.0 you can heal while driving.
- On Switch 2, with Motion Patterns on, you heal by tilting the left Joy-Con 2 back toward you.
- Guides telling you to stock up on MaxDocs predate 2.0.

title: Can I reset my perks and attributes?
body:
**Perks are refunded for free, one by one, whenever you want. Attributes reset only once per character.**

- The button to reset attributes is in the lower-left corner of the Attribute menu, and it disappears once you use it.
- It seems to be offered on brand-new 2.x saves too, but CDPR doesn't confirm it.
- Refund perks that depend on another one first.
- There is no known way to reset skills (Netrunner, Engineer…).
- **Make a manual save before resetting attributes.**
- If a guide talks about paying eddies or about the Tabula e-Rasa shard, it predates 2.0.

title: A door or a dialogue asks for Body or Technical Ability I don't have. Am I missing something?
body:
**It almost never blocks the story: there is usually another way in (a vent, a window, another door, a quickhack or a key) or another dialogue option.**

- Body forces doors open and rips off turrets; Technical Ability picks some locks and tampers with devices; Intelligence accesses local subnets.
- In Act 1, the hard checks were in The Pickup. The Heist has Intelligence options and one Cool 5 line.
- Gorilla Arms (from level 10) add 1 to 6 to Body checks.
- A hacker benefits from raising Technical Ability toward 9 anyway (for All Things Cyber), and that covers many early doors.
- Some optional loot behind 18–20 doors may stay locked.

title: Why are the police chasing me, and how do I lose them?
body:
**Since 2.0 the NCPD chases you when you commit a crime, such as attacking civilians or officers, or running them over while driving.** Your wanted level goes from 1 to 5 stars; at 5, MaxTac arrives.

- They take no bribes and don't let you surrender. Leave the search zone on foot or by car and **stay out of their sight**.
- You can also hide inside the zone, but they take longer to stop looking.
- You can quickhack officers.
- Shooting enemies who are already hostile doesn't draw the police. Watch out for stray bullets and for quickhacks that spread to whoever is nearby.
- Since 2.2, repainting your car with CrystalCoat lowers your wanted level, but only on some brands; your Archer Hella doesn't seem to be one of them.

title: I finished The Pickup. What's next? The next mission doesn't show up.
body:
**All that's left is The Information, which starts at Lizzie's Bar between 6:00 PM and 6:00 AM.** Once both are done, call Dex and The Heist begins.

- The Pickup ends with "Call Dex" and "Talk to Dex": if nothing new shows up, check that you made that call, open the journal and track the job.
- During the day you can't progress at Lizzie's: skip time to the night.
- IGN gives it a recommended level of 3, so at level 5 you are fine.
- There's no rush with The Heist: it starts at the Afterlife, and at that briefing you can still walk away to do other things.

title: It tells me to wait for a call or for the lockdown to end, and nothing happens. How do I skip time?
body:
**Open the game menu and pick Skip Time, bottom left next to the clock; move the blue dot to the hour you want.** On a controller the menu usually opens with START; on Switch 2 probably with +. Check it.

- You only skip whole hours; going all the way round skips a full day.
- Sleeping in your bed also passes time and gives a skill XP bonus.
- **"Wait for the lockdown to end" in The Gig is normal:** the Watson lockdown lifts after The Heist, so it sits in the journal all of Act 1.
- For slow calls in Act 2, get away from the job's area and skip 24 hours.
- Careful: some jobs fail if you leave or wait too long; read the objective first.

title: NCPD hustles don't show up on my map. Where are they?
body:
**They start by proximity: the icon only shows on the minimap when you are close.** To see them all, pick the custom filter on the map and turn on NCPD Scanner (the exact menu names may vary).

- They come in several types: Assault in Progress, Reported Crime, Suspected Organized Crime Activity and Cyberpsycho Sightings.
- Some crimes start when you read a shard or an NCPD message.
- Once done, they don't come back.
- Watson's are available now and their difficulty scales with you.
- Some players say certain hustles only appear at night or later in the story; that isn't confirmed.

title: Which of Regina's gigs can I do before The Heist? Why won't she give me more?
body:
**All 23 Watson gigs seem doable in Act 1, but they arrive in sets: Regina gives you the next set only after you finish every gig in the current one.**

- The first set (tier 1): Hippocratic Oath, Many Ways to Skin a Cat, Monster Hunt, Playing for Keeps and Rite of Passage.
- Hover over Regina's icon on the map to see your progress.
- If the next set doesn't arrive, check that none of the current set is left, reply to her messages and skip time.
- Since 1.5 they need no Street Cred.
- Several players report finishing them all before The Heist; there is no official confirmation.
- One reason to leave a few: finishing them all gets you the Axolotl, which comes at a lower tier if you get it early.

title: What do I have to do in the Psycho Killer job?
body:
**Psycho Killer (es-MX «Loco un poco») is Regina Jones's job that groups the 17 cyberpsycho sightings: neutralize each one, search the area and send the information to Regina.**

- Each sighting pays separately, whether you kill them or not. Until you search the laptop or shard and send it to Regina, that sighting doesn't count.
- In Act 1 there are five in Watson: Demons of War, Lt. Mower, Six Feet Under, Ticket to the Major Leagues and Where the Bodies Hit the Floor. Bloody Ritual needs Act 2 (8 PM to 5 AM); The Wasteland, Life During Wartime; the rest, Act 2.
- None is missable before the final point of no return.
- After all 17, Regina leaves the final reward (per the wiki: Chrome Compressor, the Pax mod, a capacity shard and a Trauma Team jacket; another page doesn't list the Chrome Compressor). If you kept them alive, she thanks you. Achievement: "I Am The Law".

title: What do I miss if I do The Heist now? What level should I be?
body:
**In Watson, almost nothing: whatever you leave undone is still there in Act 2. What you can lose is inside The Heist itself.** No source gives a recommended level; this guide suggests getting close to 10.

- Inside: Kongou (by Yorinobu's bed), Satori (in Saburo's AV on the roof pad), Nehan (on Saburo's body), the Iguana Egg (behind the tree trunk), Yorinobu's clothes and the Kotetsu no Ryu coat.
- Before going in, decide where Jackie's body goes.
- Still there afterwards: cyberpsychos, Watson gigs and hustles, Viktor's debt, The Gun and The Gift.
- Apartments and tarot cards come in Act 2.
- At the Afterlife briefing, "Something I gotta take care of first" lets you walk away; "Let's go" commits you.

title: I spared Brick in The Pickup. Which Act 1 choices change anything later?
body:
**Few, and almost all are in The Pickup and The Heist.** There is no overall "karma".

- **Brick freed:** only happens on paths 3 and 4. If Royce died, Brick shows up again in Second Conflict (Kerry's chain, Act 2) and lets you leave in peace; on path 3 you never see him again. On path 4, Maelstrom ambushes you later while you drive around Watson.
- **Meredith:** if she (not Gilchrist) met you at the All Foods gate, she may text you in Act 2 for an encounter (Venus in Furs). Sources disagree on whether you had to accept her chip.
- **Chaos:** you only have it if Royce died.
- **Jackie's body**, in The Heist, changes how long Heroes is.
- Viktor's debt only locks his services, and Evelyn's offer to cut Dex out changes nothing.

title: Can romances be missed? Can I change V's body or voice?
body:
**Body type and voice tone can't be changed after creating V, and each romance needs a specific one.** Everything else about the look can be changed at a mirror or a ripperdoc.

- Judy: feminine body and voice. River: feminine body. Panam: masculine body. Kerry: masculine body and voice.
- Lifepath and genitals don't matter. You can have two at once with no consequences (Panam and Kerry, or River and Judy).
- Each chain has points where it can be lost, all in Act 2.
- Nothing romance-related happens in Act 1, except setting up the Meredith encounter, which works with any V.
- Since 2.1 you can hang out with your partner at the apartment.

title: When does Phantom Liberty start? Do I need a certain level?
body:
**In Act 2, after the Voodoo Boys chain: when Transmission is done, Songbird calls and Dog Eat Dog begins.** There is no level requirement and it can't be started from Act 1.

- First you have to finish The Heist, Playing for Time, Automatic Love, The Space in Between, Disasterpiece, Double Life, M'ap Tann Pèlen and I Walk the Line.
- Turning down Songbird's first call doesn't lock you out.
- The Relic tree opens in Dog Eat Dog.
- There is a skip-ahead start for a new game (at level 20, per rpgsite), but you lose the Act 1 and 2 choices and iconics. With your save, just play normally.

title: Do I have Update 2.5 on my Switch 2 yet?
body:
**Yes: 2.5 (Edgerunners 2) reached Switch 2 on 27 October 2026, five days after PC and the other consoles.** If you don't have it, update the game from the HOME menu; the version shows in the game's main menu.

- It brings the same as on PS5: dual wield (Double Trouble), glamdocs, new tarot cards, clothing sets, stash filters and saves grouped by playthrough.
- The new quests, Clampdown and Welcome to Paradise, need The Heist done: in Act 1 you won't see them yet.
- It fixes the Switch 2 "Save failed - insufficient space" error.
- The official notes list mods (mod.io) on Switch 2, though some sources leave it out: look for the mods tab in the main menu.
- The field of view (FOV) slider was added "on consoles"; on Switch 2 it isn't confirmed.

title: Quality or Performance mode on Switch 2?
body:
**In handheld, Performance feels smoother. On a TV, use Quality, unless your TV is 120 Hz.**

- Quality: 30 fps at 1080p, on TV and in handheld.
- Performance: up to 40 fps, at 1080p on TV and 720p in handheld, with VRR in handheld.
- On a TV the Switch 2 has no VRR: without a 120 Hz screen, 40 fps looks worse in motion than 30.
- In shootouts, while driving and in Dogtown (Phantom Liberty), Performance can drop to 30 or lower.
- With gyro, more fps makes aiming feel better.
- You change it in the game's settings.

title: How do I make gyro work only while aiming? What else helps if my aim is weak?
body:
**In Settings → Controls, set Gyroscope Mode to "When holding aim button": gyro then only works while you aim a ranged weapon.** The menu names are given in English because their Latin-American Spanish text is not confirmed.

- The five options: Disabled, Always enabled, Always enabled except in menus, With ranged weapons and When holding aim button.
- Gyro uses the right Joy-Con 2. Lower the sensitivity and raise movement dampening.
- In Accessibility: ranged Aim Assist on Substantial and Snap to Target on.
- Raise Zoom Sensitivity Reduction so the camera moves slower while aiming.
- The best help is not needing to aim: a quickhack only needs a scan and a pick, and Smart Link aims for you.

title: Which button scans and hacks on Switch 2?
body:
**You scan by holding the left shoulder button: L1 on PlayStation and LB on Xbox; on Switch 2 it should be L.** Check it in Settings → Controls: we found no official Switch 2 button list.

- While scanning, you pick the quickhack from the enemy's or device's list.
- In handheld you can also tap the screen in menus, the map, the perk tree and the inventory.
- Update 2.5 fixed a bug where tagging enemies while scanning made V crouch or stand up with some control schemes.
- In mouse mode, per one review, firing moves from ZR to R.

title: What are Motion Patterns for, and why is the option grayed out?
body:
**The option (Motion Patterns) stays grayed out until you finish its tutorial in The Rescue, with a shard Jackie gives you.** After that you can replay the tutorial from Controls.

- It only works with both Joy-Con 2 detached, without a grip.
- Dodge: rotate the left Joy-Con 2 toward the direction. Use a consumable (heal): tilt the left one back toward you.
- Fast melee: turn the right one inward. Strong melee: tilt the right one back, then slap it down.
- Reload: rotate the right one clockwise.
- Per one review, the reload twist sometimes points the camera at the ceiling; if it bothers you, turn them off.

title: Can I have Latin-American Spanish text with voices in another language?
body:
**Yes, and on Switch 2 that's the default: Latin-American Spanish is text only, with no voices.** Voices come in English, or you can download a free voice pack, such as Castilian (Spain) Spanish.

- The voice packs are on the eShop for free and take up to 2.9 GB each.
- They install to the console's memory or the microSD card, even if you have the game card.
- The language settings have separate voice-over, subtitle and interface options; per one guide, they only appear in the main menu settings.
- Spanish text doesn't have the English-strings bug that affects some other languages.

title: How many save slots are there? Are saves stored in the cloud?
body:
**There are 20 manual saves, 20 autosaves and 10 quicksaves. With Nintendo Switch Online you get cloud saves, and CDPR's cross-progression keeps another copy.**

- For cross-progression, link a CD PROJEKT RED account from the Load Game screen, with the button in the bottom left; it's toggled in the Gameplay settings. It keeps the latest save of each type.
- Since 2.5, saves are grouped by playthrough.
- Update 2.5 fixed the Switch 2 "Save failed - insufficient space" error; if you still get it, free up space on the console or the microSD card.
- CDPR recommends saving often and keeping more than one backup file.

title: The game crashes or freezes on Switch 2. What do I do?
body:
**Check for corrupt data, clear the cache, restart and load an earlier save.** These are CDPR support's steps.

- System Settings → Data Management → Manage Software → Cyberpunk 2077 → Check for Corrupt Data.
- System Settings → System → Formatting Options → Clear Cache. It doesn't delete your saves. Then restart.
- If the console freezes, hold the Power button for 12 seconds or more, take out the game card or microSD card, power on, update the system and try again.
- Stutter when loading areas while driving, and in Dogtown, is still reported.

title: You are locked in Watson until The Heist
body:
During Act 1 you can only explore **Watson**: the district is closed off for Saburo Arasaka's visit to Konpeki Plaza. Watson does not close later; it is the other way round: **you are locked inside Watson until The Heist**, and the rest of Night City opens in Act 2. Watson stays reachable after that.

- Since 2.0, **all enemies scale to your level**: difficulty no longer depends on the district.
- Loot and vendor stock also scale with your level.
- Watson's five ripperdocs, the Cyberpsycho Sightings, Regina's gigs and the NCPD Scanner Hustles are already within reach.

Use this stretch to level up and gear up before The Heist: afterwards the story keeps you away from shops for a good while.

title: Start The Heist around level 10
body:
No source gives a recommended level for The Heist: IGN's table shows "-" and game8 gives none. Enemies scale with you, so you do not need to be over-levelled. Even so, you should start it **around level 10**:

- Level 10 unlocks **Tier 2 cyberware**: Reinforced Tendons, Memory Boost, Optical Camo, Synaptic Accelerator and the Biotech Σ cyberdeck. Tier 2 weapons arrive from level 9.
- **Intelligence 9** opens Hack Queue and the Embedded Exploit branch.
- About €$11,000 covers Reinforced Tendons, which cost about €$10,700.
- The Heist is long, and what follows, Love Like Fire and Playing for Time, gives you no shopping stops.

To get there, do the five Act 1 Cyberpsycho Sightings, Regina's gigs and the NCPD Scanner Hustles: they give XP and eddies. **Save manually before you go in**: there are missable weapons inside.

title: Cyberpsychos and Regina's gigs
body:
**Cyberpsycho Sightings (Psycho Killer):** they start with Regina's call after The Ripperdoc and Jackie's talk in The Ride. Act 1 has **five in Watson**: Demons of War (after The Pickup), Lt. Mower, Six Feet Under, Ticket to the Major Leagues and Where the Bodies Hit the Floor; together they pay about €$13,000. The sixth Watson one, Bloody Ritual, needs Act 2, from 8 PM to 5 AM. **Incapacitate them instead of killing them** for Regina's better reaction, and don't hit them once they're down; the reward comes either way.

**Regina's gigs:** Watson has 23, tiers 1 to 8 (the gig's difficulty, not your level). They arrive **in sets**: Regina gives you the next set only after you finish every gig in the current one. Since 1.5 they need no Street Cred. The first set: Hippocratic Oath, Many Ways to Skin a Cat, Monster Hunt, Playing for Keeps and Rite of Passage. Several players report doing them all before The Heist.

Finishing all the Watson gigs triggers Last Call, which leaves the **Axolotl** in your stash. Its Tier 5 needs level 33: finish them very early and you get a lower tier. That's one reason to leave a few for Act 2; per one player, Johnny also comments on one or two if you do them later (unconfirmed).

title: Making eddies in Watson
body:
- **NCPD Scanner Hustles** (blue map markers): Watson's pay €$750–2,100 each, about **€$42,000** in total, plus the loot in their caches.
- **Cyberpsycho Sightings:** the five in Act 1 pay about **€$13,000** in total.
- **Regina's gigs:** the five tier 1 gigs pay about €$14,000; Last Login, €$6,400.
- **Sell junk and loot you don't use** at Drop Points (Sell All Junk) and to vendors. Since 2.0 loot scales with your level.
- **Access points:** Breach Protocol gives eddies and components; the harder ones also give quickhacks.

The figures are wiki values and may vary with your level. Car races are Act 2.

If Royce died in The Pickup, you already collected €$3,000 for him. Brick's €$5,000 bounty only pays if you kill him with the detonator; if you let him live, there is none.

Don't count on item duplication tricks: none is confirmed for 2.5.

title: Watson's ripperdocs all sell the same
body:
Watson has five ripperdocs: **Viktor Vektor** (Little China), **Charles Bucks**, **Dr. Chrome** (Robert Rainwater) and **Instant Implants** (Sogo Watanabe) in Kabuki, and **Cassius Ryder** (Northside, Pershing St.). Viktor won't serve you until you pay his debt.

- **Since 2.0 they all have the same stock at the same prices.** No need to shop around: what they sell depends on your level and on owning Phantom Liberty. Viktor has the same minus Bionic Joints, Cogito Lattice and NeuroMatrix, which a hacker doesn't need. If an old guide says each one sells different parts, it predates 2.0.
- **Only one tier of each implant is on sale at a time:** at level 10 the Tier 1 versions disappear and Tier 2 ones appear, and so on every 10 levels. If you want something cheap at Tier 1, buy it before. The random bonuses you see don't change until then either.
- **Street Cred doesn't change ripperdoc stock**: only your level counts.
- You can only install or swap cyberware at a ripperdoc.
- **Charles Bucks** gives you a **permanent 20% discount** if you accept his bribe in the gig Last Login (Kabuki, tier 5: steal Alois Daquin's laptop; €$6,400, 1,000 XP and 770 Street Cred). Refuse and he flees; attack or kill him and you lose him as a vendor for good.
- Street Cred does give a permanent vendor discount: up to 15% at 50, the maximum.

title: Double jump: Reinforced Tendons from level 10
body:
Reinforced Tendons goes in the **Legs** slot: press jump in midair to **double jump**. It costs 8 capacity and is attuned to Reflexes (Crit Chance). Double jump is disabled after falling from too high. It gives little armor: 4 at Tier 2, up to 12 at 5++.

- **Where:** any ripperdoc (all five in Watson), **starting at level 10**; there is no Tier 1 version. **It needs no Street Cred**: ripperdoc stock depends only on your level.
- **Price:** about **€$10,700** at Tier 2, per two 2.x guides that agree; check it in game. It costs the same from level 10 to 19, because the price depends on the implant's tier, not on your level. With Charles Bucks's 20% it drops to about €$8,600, and Street Cred takes a bit more off.
- The €$45,000 in old guides is a 1.x price; IGN's €$67,824 looks like its Tier 4.
- Upgrading it later takes 1.5 times the components of a normal implant.
- 2.x build guides call it the best leg cyberware; both the netrunner and the smart-weapon builds use it.

Alternatives, also Legs and from level 10:

- **Lynx Paws** (capacity 5, attuned to Cool): you move 50% more quietly, faster while crouched, and take −20% fall damage. The stealth option.
- **Fortified Ankles** (capacity 6, attuned to Body): charge jump.

title: Cyberware capacity in Act 1
body:
**Cyberware Capacity** comes mainly from your level: 24 at level 1 and +3 per level, so you have **36 at level 5** and **51 at level 10**.

What you already wear takes about 22 (this guide's arithmetic): Viktor's Ballistic Coprocessor (2), Basic Kiroshi Optics (1) and Subdermal Armor (5), plus the Militech Paraline (14). That leaves about **14 free at level 5** and about **29 at level 10**.

**The usual hacker picks:** Reinforced Tendons 8, RAM Upgrade 8, Smart Link 4 (replacing the Ballistic Coprocessor's 2), Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics 2 (replacing 1), Memory Boost 18 and Optical Camo 20. At level 10 it won't all fit: Tendons, RAM Upgrade, Smart Link and Sentry use about 19 of your 29, and Memory Boost or the camo will have to wait a few levels or a few shards.

**Cyberware Capacity Shards:** random drops from enemies all over Night City.

- Tier 2 (+2): 7 in total, from your level 2, at most one per level.
- Tier 3 (+3): 4, from level 9. Tier 4 (+4): 4, from 17. Tier 5 (+6): 2, from 25.
- Regina's final reward for all 17 cyberpsychos holds a Tier 4 or 5 one (the Tier 5 needs your level 25).
- Phantom Liberty has a missable one: in the EBM Petrochem Stadium parking garage, during Dog Eat Dog.

Loot everyone you take down. **Other capacity sources:** the Engineer skill (+5 at its level 10 and +10 at 30; it also levels from crafting, upgrading and disassembling), Renaissance Punk (+4 per attribute at 9 or higher) and Edgerunner (Technical Ability 20). The Chrome Compressor gives a lot, but it replaces your cyberdeck: useless for a netrunner.

title: Viktor's debt: €$21,000, no deadline
body:
If you didn't pay (or couldn't) in The Ripperdoc, the job **Paid in Full** opens: you owe **Viktor** **€$21,000** for the Ballistic Coprocessor, Basic Kiroshi Optics and Subdermal Armor he installed.

- **There is no deadline.**
- **Until you pay him, his services stay locked.**
- When you have the money, go back to his clinic in Little China. Viktor will try to refuse it and V will insist.

Since in 2.x every ripperdoc sells the same stock at the same price, the debt costs you almost nothing: buy from Charles Bucks, Dr. Chrome, Instant Implants or Cassius Ryder, and pay Viktor when you have €$21,000 to spare.

**Don't pay him before buying what you need**, such as Reinforced Tendons at level 10 (about €$10,700), if you are short on eddies.

title: Your first cyberdeck and your eyes
body:
**You already have a cyberdeck:** a Tier 1 **Militech Paraline**, since The Rescue. These are sold at any ripperdoc:

- **Militech Paraline:** +10% quickhack damage from Tier 2; from Tier 4, shooting with a smart weapon speeds up a quickhack upload. The one that fits smart weapons.
- **Arasaka:** enemies take longer to trace you; the best for stealth.
- **Tetratronic Rippler:** the one that can reach the most RAM (5 to 20 depending on its tier).
- **Biotech Σ:** from level 10; longer Combat quickhacks and stronger damage over time.

**Eyes:** you already wear Basic Kiroshi Optics (part of Viktor's debt, attuned to Cool). The cheap upgrade for a hacker is **Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics**: Tier 1, capacity 2, **attuned to Intelligence**, and they highlight cameras and turrets when you scan. You have a single Face slot until Birds with Broken Wings (Phantom Liberty).

For more RAM, in the Frontal Cortex: RAM Upgrade (Tier 1, on sale from your level 1) and Memory Boost (from level 10).

title: Quickhacks in Watson: Yoko and Nix
body:
In Watson, quickhacks are sold by **Yoko Tsuru** (EdgeNet shop in Kabuki Market) and **Nix** (at the Afterlife, Little China), with the same list. It is not confirmed that Nix trades with you before The Heist. The other netrunner vendors (Chang Hoon Nam and another in Japantown, plus those in Coastview and Vista del Rey) are Act 2.

**What they sell by your level** (game data from version 2.31; 2.5 changed no vendors):

- **Always:** Tier 1 Ping, a Tier 1 Covert quickhack (apparently Bait) and netrunner clothing.
- **Crafting specs:** Tier 2 from your level 2; Tier 3 from 12; Tier 4 from 20; Tier 5 from 30.
- **Ready-made quickhacks:** Tier 2 from your level 7; Tier 3 from 15; Tier 4 from 23; Tier 5 from 32.
- Each threshold also opens if you have a higher-tier cyberdeck equipped; it looks like a Tier 2 deck brings Tier 2 quickhacks forward. Check it in game.

At Tier 2 they sell Short Circuit, Overheat, Contagion, Cyberware Malfunction, Cripple Movement, Weapon Glitch, Reboot Optics, Sonic Shock, Request Backup and Bait; Tier 3 adds Synapse Burnout, Memory Wipe and Ping. **They never sell the Tier 1 version** of Short Circuit or Overheat: those come from loot, enemy netrunners and access points. Short Circuit's first spec is Tier 3 (your level 12).

**At level 5:** buy Tier 2 specs if you have quickhack components, loot enemy netrunners and come back at level 7. To craft a quickhack you need its spec and quickhack components, which enemy netrunners and access points drop (vendors no longer sell them). No perk is needed, and crafting quickhacks levels the Netrunner skill.

title: Free items you can get now
body:
- **Dying Night** (iconic Power pistol): free from Robert Wilson at 2nd Amendment, Megabuilding H10 (job The Gun).
- **Ping** (quickhack): free from Yoko Tsuru at the EdgeNet shop in Kabuki Market (job The Gift).
- **Synapse Burnout** (Tier 3 Combat quickhack): from The Pickup, if you breached the Militech shard and copied the infected data. It costs 10 RAM and your Tier 1 Paraline has 5 base RAM: keep it until you have more RAM (Intelligence, Frontal Cortex cyberware, another deck) or Overclock, at Intelligence 15.
- **Chaos** (iconic Tech pistol): only if Royce died in The Pickup. Brick can only be freed on paths 3 and 4, so if you saved him you most likely have it already.

**In The Heist** you will find **Kongou** (iconic Power pistol), **Satori** (iconic katana) and **Nehan** (iconic throwing knife). **They are missable.** With Phantom Liberty, Herold Lowe sells them later, but don't rely on it: save first and look for them.

title: Skippy waits for Act 2
body:
**Skippy** (iconic smart pistol) lies beside a body in an alley in **Vista del Rey, Heywood**, so you can only fetch it in Act 2. Pick it up as soon as the city opens:

- **It needs no Smart Link** to lock on.
- Choose its mode: **Puppy-Loving Pacifist** (limbs only, non-lethal) or **Stone Cold Killer** (head when you aim).
- For a player with weak aim, it is the best weapon of the early game.
- It doesn't work for dual wielding: Double Trouble only takes Power pistols and revolvers.

**Overture** is not an iconic in 2.x: it is a regular Power revolver that Robert Wilson (Little China) and other vendors stock from level 17.

Jackie's items come after The Heist, and Dex's Plan B after Act 1.

title: Attributes, levels and perk points
body:
- **Six attributes:** Body, Reflexes, Technical Ability, Intelligence, Cool and **Relic** (Phantom Liberty only).
- At character creation you have 3 in each and 7 points to place (max 6 at creation). After that, the cap is **20**.
- **Every level gives +1 attribute point and +1 perk point.** Each skill also gives +1 perk point at its levels 15 and 35.
- **Level cap: 60** with Phantom Liberty, included in the Ultimate Edition (50 without it).

What each point gives: Body +2 max Health; Reflexes +0.5% Crit Chance; Technical Ability +2 Armor; Intelligence +1 max RAM per 4 points; Cool +1.25% Crit Damage.

Since 2.0 cyberware is **attuned to an attribute**: the higher that attribute, the stronger its bonus. Smart Link and Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics, for example, go with Intelligence.

**Skills** (Headhunter, Netrunner, Shinobi, Solo, Engineer) level by use up to 60, independent of the attribute. Netrunner levels with quickhacks, daemons, Smart-weapon or Monowire kills and crafting quickhacks; it gives +1 RAM at its levels 10 and 30.

title: The Intelligence tree for a hacker
body:
The milestones that matter, by Intelligence level:

- **Intelligence 4:** Optimization (+35% RAM recovery), which opens Proximate Propagation, Encryption (−30% traceability) and Subordination. Separately, Eye In The Sky highlights access points and cameras and makes quickhacks sent through cameras cheaper.
- **Intelligence 9:** **Hack Queue**: +1 RAM and, at its second level, **queues: two quickhacks in a row on the same enemy**. **Embedded Exploit**, which needs Optimization: **+60% quickhack damage** against targets under Control, Covert or Distract quickhacks. From it come Shadowrunner, ICEpick, System Overwhelm and Speculation. Counter-A-Hack lets you hack enemy netrunners through walls.
- **Intelligence 15:** **Overclock**, which needs Embedded Exploit: you cast quickhacks without enough RAM, and each missing RAM unit costs 10 Health; it lasts 14 s with a 30 s cooldown. The mode unlocks at the perk's **level 3** and needs a cyberdeck in the Operating System slot. Per one guide, on a controller you activate it with L1 + R1 (PlayStation) or LB + RB (Xbox) together; on Switch 2 it should be L + R (check it in Settings → Controls). **Queue Acceleration** adds one more quickhack to the queue.
- **Intelligence 20:** **Spillover** (while Overclock is active, +50% chance for a quickhack to spread to another target), **Queue Mastery** and Smart Synergy.

For RAM recovery: Optimization, Embedded Exploit, Feedback Loop, the Netrunner skill, RAM Upgrade, Memory Boost and Feen-X.

title: Technical Ability and cyberware capacity
body:
**Cyberware Capacity** comes mainly from your level: 24 at level 1, +3 per level, 201 at 60. Capacity Shards, the Engineer skill, Edgerunner and the Chrome Compressor add more. The cyberware perks are in **Technical Ability**:

- **Technical Ability 9: All Things Cyber**: +10% to all your cyberware's stats and −20% capacity cost for Integumentary and Skeleton cyberware. From it: Driver Update (+1 stat modifier on every implant), Chipware Connoisseur (you choose between stat modifiers when upgrading) and Renaissance Punk (+4 capacity per attribute at 9 or higher).
- **Technical Ability 15: License To Chrome**: +10% cyberware stats, +40 Armor and a **third Skeleton slot**. And **Ambidextrous**: a **second Hands slot**.
- **Technical Ability 20: Edgerunner**: lets you exceed capacity by up to 50 at −0.5% max Health per point over; kills can trigger Fury (more damage and crits for 12 s).

For healing: Glutton For War (Technical Ability 4) and Health Freak (Technical Ability 9). Since 2.0 health items work with charges that recharge on their own.

Cyberware is only installed or upgraded at a ripperdoc. Upgrading costs **crafting components and eddies**; no level requirement is known, and in the Crafting menu you turn 5 components of one tier into 1 of the next.

title: Components, upgrades and crafting
body:
Since 2.0, crafting and upgrading use **crafting components** of a single type per tier. You get them by disassembling weapons and clothes, and from loot. In the Crafting menu you can turn **5 components of one tier into 1 of the next**. Lucky Day (Technical Ability 9) gives +25% components from looting.

**Iconic weapons:** the only weapons that can be upgraded. Go to the Crafting menu, Upgrades tab, with the weapon in your inventory; stashed ones don't show up. It needs no perks or specs.

- From a tier to its "+": 75 components of that tier (Tier 1 to 1+, 75 Tier 1).
- From "+" to the next tier: 40 components of the next tier (1+ to 2, 40 Tier 2).
- The last step, 5+ to 5++: 200 Tier 5 (needs Phantom Liberty).

Normal weapons can't be upgraded: replace them with higher-tier ones.

**Cyberware:** upgraded at the ripperdoc with components and eddies; no level requirement is known. Each implant multiplies the base cost (Reinforced Tendons ×1.5; Lynx Paws ×0.5).

**Sell or disassemble?**

- Junk is only good for selling (Drop Points: Sell All Junk).
- Disassemble clothes you don't wear: they sell for little and the Wardrobe keeps their look.
- Sell weapons when you are short on eddies and disassemble them when you are short on components.
- Since 2.1 you can mark weapons as favorites: then they can't be sold, disassembled or dropped by mistake.

Crafting, upgrading and disassembling give Engineer skill XP.

title: Quickhacks and combos
body:
- **Types:** Combat (damage), Control (disable or distract), Covert (low RAM and rarely traced), Ultimate (the most expensive), Device (built into the cyberdeck) and Vehicle (needs Carhacker).
- **Where to get them:** netrunner vendors (in Watson, Yoko Tsuru and Nix: Tier 2 quickhacks from your level 7, and never the Tier 1 version of Short Circuit or Overheat), enemy netrunners, Airdrops and the harder access points. Since 2.0 vendors no longer sell quickhack crafting components.
- **Breach Protocol now works on access points only**, not on enemies.
- **Before casting:** you need enough RAM and, generally, to see the target, directly or through a camera. Some enemies resist quickhacks and cost more RAM.
- **Trace:** Combat and Control quickhacks fill a trace bar; if it completes, enemies know where you are. Encryption, Shadowrunner (with takedowns), Memory Wipe and Sonic Shock (which are untraceable) and the Arasaka cyberdeck keep it down.

**Combos:**

- **Contagion → Overheat:** Contagion poisons and spreads to 2 nearby enemies (4 from its Tier 3); from its Tier 4, Burn or Overheat detonates it. For groups; it doesn't work on mechs or drones.
- **Stacked Cyberware Malfunction → Short Circuit**, which also hits mechs, drones and turrets harder.
- **Memory Wipe first**, to stop traces.
- Synapse Burnout + Overheat, and Cripple Movement + Cyberware Malfunction.
- For stealth, the untraceable ones: System Collapse, Memory Wipe and Sonic Shock.

Note: since 2.02, Tier 5 Memory Wipe costs too much RAM to use.

title: Smart weapons and Smart Link
body:
**Smart weapons** fire guided rounds that **lock on and seek** targets inside the weapon's tracking box: they curve around obstacles and travel slower than normal bullets. Hits are not guaranteed; a better Smart Link tracks better. They take no suppressors or scopes, and Tyger Claws' masking-ink tattoos give smart rounds a 50% miss chance.

- **In 2.x you need a Smart Link** (or the Tyger Claws tattoo, below) to lock on. The exception is **Skippy**, which needs nothing.
- Smart Link goes in the **Hands** slot: Tier 1, capacity 4, attuned to Intelligence, +1 or +2 max RAM. Any ripperdoc sells it.
- **It shares the single Hands slot with the Ballistic Coprocessor** Viktor installed: you have to swap one for the other until you have Ambidextrous (Technical Ability 15).
- **Tattoo: Tyger Claws Dermal Imprint** (Hands, capacity 0) also enables lock-on. Cassius Ryder gives it to you after The Gig, in Act 2; from its Tier 3 it locks on faster.
- Since 2.0 they deal less damage, but they have their own Intelligence branch: Acquisition Specialist, Target Lock Transfer, Targeting Prism (multiple targets when aiming) and Smart Synergy (instant lock during Overclock).
- Without those perks, reloading or switching weapons can break the lock.
- Tier 3 Ping: +25% lock-on speed against pinged targets.

With smart SMGs and pistols plus quickhacks, you barely have to aim.

title: Two pistols with Double Trouble (2.5)
body:
Update 2.5 added **dual wield** with **Double Trouble**, a **Cool 9** perk with no prerequisite perk.

- **Power pistols and revolvers only.** It doesn't work with Tech or smart weapons (not Skippy, not King's Coronation), other weapon types, or melee.
- **Level 1:** you carry two guns that fire together, at **−37.5% damage each**; when aiming, −15% recoil and spread.
- **Level 2:** the **Heywood Hurricane** replaces Quick Melee: it fires both guns for 1 s at +50% spread and refunds the ammo of hits.
- **How to equip them:** in the inventory, set a Power pistol or revolver as your primary weapon and use the **secondary weapon slot that appears on the left**. You can mix a pistol and a revolver; you don't need two of the same.
- **Support perks** (Cool 9, need Double Trouble): Two Right Hands, Triple Tequila, Splash Of Love and Keep 'Em Comin'.

IGN's pairings: Riskit and Death and Taxes, Seraph and Unity, Her Majesty and Mancinella. From Act 1 you have Dying Night and Kongou at hand. Johnny's Malorian Arms 3516 (Act 2) is a Power pistol, but its effect is on Quick Melee, exactly what the Hurricane replaces (this guide's deduction).

The Hurricane fires from the hip and needs little aim, but it uses no smart rounds: for a hacker it is an extra, not the core of the build.

title: How to redistribute perks and attributes
body:
- **Perks:** you refund them **for free, any time, one by one**. There is no button to refund them all at once; refund perks that depend on another one first.
- **Attributes:** there is **one reset per character**, with the button in the lower-left corner of the Attribute menu, which disappears once used; you don't need Phantom Liberty. A 2.5 guide and some players say it is offered on new saves too; CDPR doesn't confirm it, so treat it as a one-time chance.
- **Skills:** no source mentions a way to reset them.

**Make a manual save before resetting attributes.** If the new spread doesn't convince you, reload and think it over.

Try perks freely, since refunding them costs nothing, and keep the attribute reset for a big build change, for example from netrunner to smart weapons.

If an old guide says resetting costs eddies or mentions the Tabula e-Rasa shard, that information predates 2.0.

title: The Relic tree (Phantom Liberty)
body:
The **Relic** tree unlocks on its own in **Dog Eat Dog**, when Songbird gives V new Militech software. Dog Eat Dog starts after Transmission, in Act 2: **it doesn't matter before The Heist**.

**15 Relic points:** 3 in Dog Eat Dog, 3 in Birds with Broken Wings and 9 from the Operational and Restricted Data Terminals in Dogtown.

- **Jailbreak:** new abilities for arm cyberware; with the Monowire, it lets it carry a Control quickhack.
- **Data Tunneling** (needs Jailbreak and the Monowire): Monowire hits spread its quickhack.
- **Emergency Cloaking:** Optical Camo in combat makes enemies lose you. Next is **Sensory Protocol**: when you are detected while crouched, time slows so you can escape.
- **Vulnerability Analytics:** shows weak spots on armor and cyberware. Next is Machine Learning.
- Others depend on a specific arm: Projectile Launch System, Gorilla Arms or Mantis Blades.

Netrunner order per game8: Jailbreak → Data Tunneling → Emergency Cloaking → Sensory Protocol → Vulnerability Analytics → Machine Learning. For smart weapons, Vulnerability Analytics and Machine Learning first.

title: Build: quickhack netrunner
body:
Quickhacks do the damage; the gun only finishes. Attributes per game8 (Body / Reflexes / Technical Ability / Intelligence / Cool):

- Level 1: 3 / 4 / 6 / 6 / 3. Level 10: 3 / 7 / 9 / 9 / 3.
- Level 50: 6 / 15 / 15 / 20 / 15. Level 60: 16 / 15 / 15 / 20 / 15 (the Phantom Liberty points into Body). IGN prefers Cool 20 and Body 11 at 60.

**Levels 1–15:** Intelligence 9 first (Hack Queue, Embedded Exploit), Technical Ability 9 (All Things Cyber), Reflexes toward 9 (Dash). Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics, RAM Upgrade and Smart Link, and Memory Boost from level 10; Paraline or Tetratronic Rippler. Short Circuit, Overheat, Reboot Optics, Ping, and Synapse Burnout once your RAM allows.

**Levels 15–30:** Intelligence 15 (Overclock, Queue Acceleration), Technical Ability 15 (License To Chrome). Contagion; Ex-Disk at 20; Raven Microcyber from 20 if you want spread.

**Levels 30–60:** Intelligence 20 (Queue Mastery, Spillover). Camillo RAM Manager and Pain Editor (30+), NetWatch Netdriver (40+), Cyberpsychosis and System Collapse, and Relic.

**How to play:** open with Overclock; Blood Daemon, Sublimation and Power Surge keep you alive; the Monowire, with Siphon and Finisher: Live Wire, gives RAM back; finish off with smart weapons (Genjiroh, Prototype: Shingen Mark V).

title: Build: stealth netrunner
body:
No guide has this exact build: it is the netrunner build, which already rewards staying undetected, plus stealth perks and cyberware. Play slow.

- **Attributes:** as the netrunner, but raise Cool earlier, to 15 for Ninjutsu. IGN's spread with Cool 20 fits.
- **Intelligence:** Encryption (−30% traceability), Eye In The Sky (cheaper, longer camera hacks), Embedded Exploit, Subordination and Shadowrunner (takedowns wipe trace).
- **Cool:** Feline Footwork (Cool 4), Killer Instinct (+25% damage out of combat with silenced guns, knives and axes), Ninjutsu (Cool 15), Creeping Death and Vanishing Act (automatic Optical Camo when crouch-sprinting or sliding).
- **Cyberware:** Arasaka cyberdeck (slower traces, −2 RAM for Covert quickhacks, +5 RAM per takedown); Basic Kiroshi Optics or Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics for cameras; Optical Camo and Synaptic Accelerator (slows time at 50% detection), both from level 10; Lynx Paws.
- **Quickhacks:** Memory Wipe, System Collapse, Sonic Shock, Reboot Optics and Ping.
- **Relic:** Emergency Cloaking → Sensory Protocol.

**Levels 1–15:** Intelligence 9, Feline Footwork and, at level 10, Optical Camo, Synaptic Accelerator and Lynx Paws. **15–30:** Ninjutsu and Intelligence 15. **30–60:** Intelligence 20, Cool toward 20 and Relic.

title: Build: smart-weapon gunner
body:
The most forgiving one for weak aim: the gun locks on and you just shoot. Attributes per game8 (Body / Reflexes / Technical Ability / Intelligence / Cool):

- Level 1: 3 / 6 / 4 / 6 / 3. Level 10: 3 / 9 / 4 / 12 / 3.
- Level 50: 15 / 20 / 13 / 20 / 3. Level 60: 18 / 20 / 20 / 20 / 3.

**Levels 1–15:** Smart Link right away; Intelligence from 9 to 12 by level 10; Reflexes 9 for Dash; Body 4 for Painkiller. Acquisition Specialist needs Intelligence 15, so early on you only have base lock-on. Skippy as soon as Act 2 starts.

**Levels 15–30:** Intelligence 15 (Acquisition Specialist, Target Lock Transfer, Targeting Prism, Overclock); Reflexes toward 20.

**Levels 30–60:** Intelligence 20 (Smart Synergy, Spillover), Reflexes 20 (Submachine Fun: switching SMGs auto-reloads) and Technical Ability with the Phantom Liberty points (License To Chrome, Edgerunner).

**Cyberware:** Militech Paraline, **Smart Link (required)**, Kiroshi "The Oracle" Optics, Reinforced Tendons, Ex-Disk + Memory Boost + RAM Upgrade and Electrifying Monowire.

**Weapons and quickhacks:** Yinglong and Prototype: Shingen Mark V, swapping between them for Submachine Fun; Divided We Stand; with Phantom Liberty, Pizdets and Hercules 3AX. Weapon Glitch, Ping (Tier 3 locks faster) and Short Circuit with the electric Yinglong.

title: Switch 2: settings if aiming is hard
body:
The Switch 2 version has **gyro aiming**, mouse mode with the Joy-Con 2, Motion Patterns and the **touch screen** for menus, the map, the perk tree and the inventory; per CDPR, also for Breach Protocol. Option names are given in English because their Latin-American Spanish text is not confirmed.

- **Gyro:** in Settings → Controls, set **Gyroscope Mode** to **When holding aim button**: it only works while you aim a ranged weapon. Lower the sensitivity and raise movement dampening.
- Ranged **Aim Assist**: pick **Substantial**, the highest (Off / Light / Standard / Substantial). Also turn on **Snap to Target**, which snaps to targets when you aim with firearms. Since 2.1 they are in the Accessibility tab.
- Raise **Zoom Sensitivity Reduction** so the camera moves slower while aiming.
- **Breach Protocol:** since 2.1 you can **turn off its timer** (Accessibility).
- **Graphics mode:** in handheld, Performance (up to 40 fps) makes gyro feel smoother. On a TV use Quality (30 fps), unless you have a 120 Hz screen.
- **Motion Patterns:** the option stays grayed out until you finish its tutorial in The Rescue. In mouse mode, Y sometimes doesn't reload.
- **Scanner:** hold the left shoulder button (L1/LB); on Switch 2 it should be L, unconfirmed.
- You can change the difficulty any time.

Play the hacker to aim less: a quickhack only needs a scan and a pick, and smart weapons with Smart Link do the aiming for you. Avoid headshot builds with Deadeye and Focus, which reward precise aim.
